claim: Let \((X,T)=\varprojlim (X_r,T_r)\) be an inverse sequence of nonempty compact metric dynamical systems with continuous surjective bonding maps commuting with the dynamics. If every stage \((X_r,T_r)\) is full-scattering in the open-cover sense of Huang and Ye, then \((X,T)\) is full-scattering. Consequently, every countable Cartesian product of full-scattering compact metric dynamical systems is full-scattering, because its finite coordinate products are full-scattering by Xu's 2026 finite-product theorem and the full countable product is their surjective inverse limit.
integrity: The proof is self-contained apart from the explicitly cited finite-product theorem used only for the countable-product corollary. Search non-hits are treated as residual novelty evidence, not as proof of uniqueness.
scientific_limitations: The inverse-limit theorem assumes nonempty compact metric stages and surjective bonding maps.
The proof is qualitative and does not provide a universal divergence rate for open-cover complexity.
The countable-product corollary depends on the cited finite-product theorem for full-scattering systems.
title: Surjective inverse limits preserve full-scattering
